# Activation Clause

Maintains one party roster, an acceptance boundary and an access guard for the executing document. Its state lives at `/activation`; an embedded instruction uses its own document, not its parent's state. Hosted bootstrap resolves account locators into authenticated transports before initialization. Party descriptions and read access do not themselves establish authority to perform every operation.

## Configuration

Configuration is supplied through the clause's `parameters`; runtime functions read `/clauses/activation/parameters`.

- `parties` must be a nonempty map. Each party needs `lead.channel` and may include `displayName`, `partyId`, `business`, `readerKeys` and additional `representatives`. Business details include `displayName`, `jurisdiction` and `registrationId`. Representatives may have `displayName`, `representativeId`, `channel` and `readerKeys`. Party and representative keys must be nonempty text without `.`, `/`, `~` or `__`. Lead transports use the party key; additional transports use `party__representative`.
- `required` identifies the parties whose lead acceptance is needed; initialization defaults it to all configured party keys. `revision` defaults to `1`. Initial `approved` is empty.
- `accessPaths` defaults to `[]` and identifies embedded Timeline Access documents. `readers` defaults to `{}` and supplies groups of alternative reader keys. Party groups use `party.readerKeys`; additional representative groups use their own `readerKeys`. These roster-derived groups replace equally named entries from `readers`.
- `allowNewParties` defaults to `false`. `frozen` defaults to `false`, but initialization also freezes the roster when `/partyRosterFrozen` is true. Freezing blocks party changes and approved admission, not acceptance.
- `preActivationOperations` and `preActivationChannels` default to empty lists. They permit specified external operations and non-external deliveries before acceptance is complete, subject to the access and closure guards below. Generated acceptance, party-management and negotiation operations are also registered for this purpose. The approved-admission function requires nonempty `admission.approvers`.
- `negotiation.allowedPaths` defaults to `[]`. A nonempty list enables negotiation and requires nonempty `required` and a document `type`. Paths must be distinct absolute paths with no empty segments or `~`. They cannot start with `clauses`, `contracts`, `activation`, `clauseRuntime`, `type`, `name` or `description`, or identify an `accessPaths` location or its descendants. Each selected value must initially exist and be text, integer, double or Boolean.

The transition hook rejects edits to this clause entry in favor of its party operations. Before first activation with negotiation enabled, it also rejects changes to the overall `clauses` configuration.

## Access and activation state

Every transport must be an External Channel or Timeline Channel. External Channel transports bypass the Timeline Access coverage check. For each Timeline Channel transport, one tracked access document must contain its exact timeline, match its provider and contain at least one alternative key from **every** reader group. Empty groups fail this check; keys spread across separate documents do not satisfy this single-document requirement.

Configured access documents are embedded, and `Clauses Initialized` and embedded `Timeline Access Updated` events refresh activation. Initial party transports remain pending until access is ready. Permission changes remain provider-owned: executed, authenticated access histories establish permission, while an access request does not.

`accessReady` and `functional` express the same coverage result. Current-revision pending admissions also contribute their proposed parties to this check. `termsAccepted` requires every `required` party's approval and agreement between the actual document fields and `/activation/terms/fields`. `active` additionally requires access readiness and that `closed` is not true. `everActivated` records whether a committed state has ever been active and remains true through later suspension.

The maintained `status` distinguishes:

- `WAITING_FOR_ACCESS`: access is missing before first activation.
- `SUSPENDED_ACCESS`: access is missing after an earlier activation.
- `AWAITING_ACCEPTANCE`: access is ready, but required acceptance or agreement with recorded terms is incomplete.
- `ACTIVE`: access and acceptance are ready and the document is not closed.
- `CLOSED`: `closed` is true, taking precedence over the other statuses.

`reason` is `PARTICIPANT_ACCESS_MISSING`, `ACCEPTANCE_REQUIRED` or empty according to access and acceptance; it does not independently indicate closure. `Document Activated` marks first activation. `Document Access Suspended` marks loss of access from an active state. `Document Access Restored` is emitted when a previously activated document becomes active after access failure.

The dispatch policy allows initialization and registered embedded access-update deliveries even while access is unavailable or the document is closed. Other deliveries require initialized state, recorded and freshly checked access readiness, and an open document. Pre-activation allowances then bypass the acceptance requirement. Registered admission-consent operations have a separate exception requiring an exact match to the pending admission, revision, token, operation and channel. Remaining business deliveries require business readiness. A denied external input is still consumed and checkpointed; restoring access does not replay it.

## Acceptance and negotiation

Generated `approve_<role>`, `updateParty_<role>` and negotiation operations require `call/requireExactDocumentVersion` to be true. Their channel bindings and guards determine authority; their existence does not establish a viewer's permission.

`approve_<role>` is lead-only. It checks the current `revision`, participant access and any supplied `termsRef`; `termsRef` is required when negotiation is enabled. A new approval records that party's acceptance and emits `Terms Accepted`. An already recorded approval returns without another acceptance event. One approval does not establish unanimous acceptance. If approving current terms makes the document active, any pending proposal is closed as `SUPERSEDED` and negotiation becomes noneditable.

`terms.ref` identifies the published definition and agreed scalar fields. Initialization creates `termsRevision = 1` and negotiation state with `revision = 1`, `editable = true`, and empty `proposal`, `history` and `outcomes`. These are initialization effects, not meanings of missing state.

Negotiation operations are installed for the required approvers:

- `proposeChanges` requires the current `baseTermsRef`, a nonempty `changes` list and a unique nonempty `proposalId` without `/` or `~`. Each Term Change supplies `path` and `replacement`. Paths must be allowed and unrepeated, replacements must retain the current primitive kind, and the resulting document must satisfy its type. Unchanged terms are rejected. Replacing a different pending proposal requires its identifier in `supersedes`, closing it as `SUPERSEDED`. An identical repeat of the same proposal preserves its approvals; conflicting reuse is rejected.
- `activate` selects a `termsRef`. Current terms require omission of `proposalId` and delegate to current-term approval. Proposed terms require the matching pending identifier and reference; the stored offer's base, fields, document validity and identity are checked again. Each call records only the invoking approver's approval. Once every configured approver has approved, the proposal is applied, its approvals become current acceptances, activation and terms revisions advance, negotiation becomes noneditable, and its outcome is `APPLIED`.
- `proposeAndActivate` proposes changes and records the caller's approval in the same operation; it does not bypass other approvers.
- `withdrawAcceptance` removes the caller's acceptance of the explicitly selected current or proposed terms. `withdrawProposal` requires the recorded proposer; `rejectProposal` is available to a required approver. Closing clears the pending proposal and records `WITHDRAWN` or `REJECTED`.

New proposals, proposal withdrawal/rejection and acceptance withdrawal are blocked once `everActivated` is true, including during later access suspension. Missing or changed references, stale revisions, frozen terms, invalid replacements and conflicting identifiers are rejected rather than treated as acceptance.

## Party changes and admission

`updateParty` defaults the optional `party` target to the invoking party. A lead may replace its own party record, or add a new explicitly named party when `allowNewParties` permits it; it cannot manage another existing party. The replacement needs `lead.channel`, valid representative names and sufficient access coverage. No revision argument is required, but exact-document review is. A successful update installs the roster's channels and handlers, clears all current approvals, increments activation `revision` and emits `Party Changed`. A directly added party is appended to `required`.

Roster or required-party changes also change the terms identity and advance `termsRevision`. They close a pending proposal as `AUTHORITY_CHANGED`; when negotiation is enabled, they clear current acceptances.

`Party Addition Requested` initiates access preparation for an approved admission. Stale-revision or repeated requests are ignored. Supplied access documents must carry initialization and provider-history evidence and preserve the native executable permission policy; installation accepts 1–16 documents per call and deduplicates their original identities. Missing coverage can emit `Party Access Update Requested` for existing-party transports. Each request selects one transport, while its readiness requires coverage of every transport of the parent party. These requests grant neither access nor participant consent.

`admitApprovedParties` separately checks an unfrozen roster, matching `expectedRevision`, configured admission approvers, consistent existing main identities and sufficient access. Existing identities must retain the exact lead channel and primary reader-key set. Successful admission installs new parties and advances activation revision; it does not itself add them to `required` or record their consent.
